A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FlexTok research work. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material across appendix and figure renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction, class-conditional and text-conditional generation experiments, linear probing, scaling studies and tokenizer ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds reconstruction/generation metric tables and qualitative REPA ablation results.

M1.justification: The register encoder, FSQ bottleneck, causal masking, nested dropout, rectified-flow decoder, REPA loss and autoregressive generation procedures are unchanged. The added REPA examples evaluate an existing component.

E1.justification: Both versions retain ImageNet-1k, DFN-2B, COCO and the same qualitative prompt and out-of-distribution examples. The added evidence uses existing reconstruction and generation tasks without expanding dataset or scenario coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same comparator set, and the TiTok/ALIT, SDXL-VAE, controlled 2D-tokenizer and ablation comparisons retain their participants. The newly cited works are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: New Tables 8–9 extend token-length evaluation with reconstruction PSNR, SSIM and LPIPS, and generation sFID, Inception score, precision and recall. Existing splits, model sizes, training budgets and inference settings are retained; this expands evaluation metrics rather than establishing retraining.

E4.justification: Appendix A.3 adds Figure 13, comparing reconstructions with and without REPA for three ImageNet examples across 1–256 tokens. This supplements the existing quantitative REPA ablation in Table 3 and Figures 11–12 with new qualitative evidence.

E5.justification: Seed-based sampling descriptions are retained, including the ten decoder seeds in Figure 8. The added tables report point estimates without introducing repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests or other uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 8–9 add concrete metric results: for example, d18-d28 reconstruction PSNR is 9.35 at one token and 17.70 at 256 tokens, while generation recall is 0.53 and 0.61, respectively. Figure 13 adds qualitative REPA findings. These extend existing evaluations; Table 1 scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical descriptions of the bottleneck, rectified-flow objective, causal attention, nested dropout and optimization are retained. No new formal assumption, theorem, proof or substantive derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the claims of flexible 1–256-token representations, coarse-to-fine visual semantics and strong autoregressive generation with few tokens. Added appendix evidence does not redefine or strengthen these core claims.

C2.justification: The new REPA examples reinforce the existing semantic-inductive-bias explanation. Interpretations concerning prompt complexity, autoregressive scaling and decoder contributions remain unchanged, as do the limitations concerning dense or structured content such as text.

D1.justification: Table 8 newly makes storage accounting explicit: each token in the 64,000-entry vocabulary occupies two bytes, with byte budgets tabulated alongside token counts. This is added documentation; implementation recipes, hyperparameters and access information otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Ge et al. (2023) as a citation for causal register attention and includes TexTok, Zha et al. (2024), in Appendix D's structured-tokenization discussion. These are limited attribution and literature-coverage additions without substantial repositioning.

P1.justification: v2 inserts an additional-metrics Appendix E, updates cross-references, adds brief REPA commentary and expands the acknowledgments. The main narrative and existing appendix prose are largely retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figure 13 and Tables 8–9, adds metric-direction arrows to existing tables, and differentiates markers in the guidance-ablation plot. Appendix figures are reflowed and renumbered, including consolidation of the text-model scaling plots; existing visual evidence is retained.

improvement.justification: Tables 8–9 make reconstruction distortion and generation quality/diversity easier to assess, while Figure 13 supplies direct visual support for the existing REPA ablation. Together with limited attribution and presentation refinements, these additions improve evidential completeness and clarity without substantially changing the method, coverage or conclusions.
